{{Short description|Concept in differential geometry}}
In [[differential geometry]] and especially [[Yang–Mills theory]], a '''(weakly) stable Yang–Mills–Higgs (YMH) pair''' is a Yang–Mills–Higgs pair around which the Yang–Mills–Higgs action functional is positively or even strictly positively curved. Yang–Mills–Higgs pairs are solutions of the [[Yang–Mills–Higgs equations]] following from them being [[local extrema]] of the [[Curvature form|curvature]] of both fields, hence [[Critical point (mathematics)|critical points]] of the Yang–Mills-Higgs action functional, which are determined by a vanishing first [[derivative]] of a [[Calculus of variations|variation]]. (Weakly) stable Yang–Mills-Higgs pairs furthermore have a positive or even strictly positive curved neighborhood and hence are determined by a positive or even strictly positive second derivative of a variation.

(Weakly) stable Yang–Mills–Higgs pairs are named after [[Yang Chen-Ning]], [[Robert Mills (physicist)|Robert Mills]] and [[Peter Higgs]].

== Definition ==
Let <math>G</math> be a [[Compact space|compact]] [[Lie group]] with [[Lie algebra]] <math>\mathfrak{g}</math> and <math>E\twoheadrightarrow B</math> be a [[Principal bundle|principal <math>G</math>-bundle]] with a compact [[Orientability|orientable]] [[Riemannian manifold]] <math>B</math> having a [[Metric (mathematics)|metric]] <math>g</math> and a [[volume form]] <math>\operatorname{vol}_g</math>. Let <math>\operatorname{Ad}(E)
:=E\times_G\mathfrak{g}</math> be its [[adjoint bundle]]. <math>\mathcal{A}
=\Omega_{\operatorname{Ad}}^1(E,\mathfrak{g})</math>, an [[Affine space|affine vector space]] (not canonically) isomorphic to <math>\Omega^1(B,\operatorname{Ad}(E))</math>, is the space of [[Connection (principal bundle)|connections]].<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |last=de los Ríos |first=Santiago Quintero |date=2020-12-16 |title=Connections on principal bundles |url=https://www.homotopico.com/assets/docs/notes/principal-connections.pdf |access-date=2024-11-09 |website=homotopico.com |at=Theorem 3.7 |language=en}}</ref> These are under the [[adjoint representation]] <math>\operatorname{Ad}</math> invariant <math>\mathfrak{g}</math>-valued ([[Lie algebra–valued differential form|Lie algebra–valued]]) [[Differential form|differential forms]] on <math>E</math> and through pullback along smooth sections   <math>B\hookrightarrow E</math> differ by <math>\operatorname{Ad}(E)</math>-valued ([[vector bundle]]–valued) differential forms on <math>B</math>.

The Yang–Mills–Higgs action functional is given by:<ref name=":10">{{cite web |title=Lecture 3: The Yang–Mills equations |url=https://empg.maths.ed.ac.uk/Activities/GT/Lect3.pdf |access-date=2024-11-24 |website=empg.maths.ed.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref>

: <math>\operatorname{YMH}\colon
\Omega_{\operatorname{Ad}}^1(E,\mathfrak{g})\times\Gamma^\infty(B,\operatorname{Ad}(E))\rightarrow\mathbb{R},
\operatorname{YMH}(A,\Phi)
:=\int_B\|F_A\|^2+\|\mathrm{d}_A\Phi\|^2\mathrm{d}\operatorname{vol}_g.</math>

A Yang–Mills–Higgs pair <math>A\in\mathcal{A}
=\Omega_{\operatorname{Ad}}^1(E,\mathfrak{g})</math> and <math>\Phi\in\Gamma^\infty(B,\operatorname{Ad}(E))</math>, hence which fulfill the [[Yang–Mills–Higgs equations]], is called stable if:<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Hu |first1=Zhi |last2=Hu |first2=Sen |date=2015-02-06 |title=Degenerate and Stable Yang-Mills-Higgs Pairs |class=math-ph |language=en |eprint=1502.01791}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last=Cheng |first=Da Rong |date=2021 |title=Stable Solutions to the Abelian Yang–Mills–Higgs Equations on S2 andT2 |url=https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1007/s12220-021-00619-y.pdf |journal=The Journal of Geometric Analysis |language=en |volume=31 |pages=9551-9572, Definition 3.1 |doi=10.1007/s12220-021-00619-y |access-date=2024-10-27}}</ref><ref name=":4">{{Cite journal |last1=Han |first1=Xiaoli |last2=Jin |first2=Xishen |last3=Wen |first3=Yang |date=2023-03-01 |title=Stability and energy identity for Yang-Mills-Higgs pairs |url= |journal=[[Journal of Mathematical Physics]] |language=en |volume=64 |issue=2 |article-number=021511 |doi=10.1063/5.0130905 |arxiv=2303.00270 |bibcode=2023JMP....64b1511H }}</ref>

: <math>\frac{\mathrm{d}^2}{\mathrm{d}t^2}\operatorname{YMH}(\alpha(t),\varphi(t))\vert_{t=0}>0</math>

for every smooth family <math>\alpha\colon
(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\rightarrow\mathcal{A}
=\Omega_{\operatorname{Ad}}^1(E,\mathfrak{g})</math> with <math>\alpha(0)=A</math> and <math>\varphi\colon
(-\varepsilon,\varepsilon)\rightarrow\Gamma^\infty(B,\operatorname{Ad}(E))</math> with <math>\varphi(0)=\Phi</math>. It is called weakly stable if only <math>\geq 0</math> holds. A Yang–Mills–Higgs pair, which is not weakly stable, is called instable. For comparison, the condition to be a Yang–Mills–Higgs pair is:

: <math>\frac{\mathrm{d}}{\mathrm{d}t}\operatorname{YMH}(\alpha(t),\varphi(t))\vert_{t=0}=0.</math>

== Properties ==

* Let <math>(A,\Phi)</math> be a weakly stable Yang–Mills–Higgs pair on <math>S^n</math>, then the following claims hold:<ref name=":4" />
** If <math>n=4</math>, then <math>A</math> is a Yang–Mills connection (<math>\mathrm{d}_A\star F_A=0</math>) as well as <math>\mathrm{d}_A\Phi=0</math> and <math>\|\Phi\|=1</math>.
** If <math>n\geq 5</math>, then <math>A</math> is flat (<math>F_A=0</math>) as well as <math>\mathrm{d}_A\Phi=0</math> and <math>\|\Phi\|=1</math>.
